labels.notes: Unmarked and partial, which is correct. deux_pushup proves the first paragraph's independence in the library's reading of defi:causalite: the 'equivalently' form, ETT.tex:245-251, with no gluing (kb/0014). deux_pushup_neither states 'neither implies the other' (l.316) as two negated universal implications over Causality ℝ, and ℝ is second countable and Hausdorff, so Lean ≥ paper in that reading. FIRST HALF: lightlikeLine is ex:causalities_lines item 2 (≤_U is x ≤ y with [x,y] ⊂ U; ≪ = ∅). It has push-up vacuously and is not plain. It is now also proved causal and absolutely minimal: lightlikeLine_absolutelyMinimalOn reuses timelikeLine_absolutelyMinimalOn, the two causal relations being definitionally equal. SECOND HALF: deuxPushup = Causality.ofRelation (extLe lt (-2) (-1)) lt with a ≪ b iff φ(a) < ψ(b). Checked by hand. ψ ≤ φ, so ≪ is transitive. φ is upper and ψ lower semicontinuous, so ≪ has open sections. extLe is a preorder containing ≪. ofRelation gives monotonicity (b) and (c). φ(-2) = 2, φ(-1) = 1, ψ(1) = 2, ψ(-1) = -1, so -2 ≤ -1 ≪ 1 and not -2 ≪ 1: push-up fails at U = ⊤. ≤ lies inside the order of ℝ, so the witness is causal. Plainness holds for every U and A. I^+(-1) = ]0,∞[ lies in closure(]0,∞[∖{1}) = closure I^+(-2), and I^-(-2) = ]-∞,-2[ ⊂ I^-(-1). Every non-empty open set holds a pair a ≪ b away from the marked points. ofRelation_causallyPlain correctly reduces U to the global relations: U open gives U ∩ closure X ⊂ closure(U ∩ X). Since plainness is proved for every U, a failure of push-up at U = ⊤ refutes the implication fully (kb/0014). NON-LOCALITY is disclosed in the title, SCOPE, the deuxPushup docstring and the REPORT (deuxPushup_not_absolutelyMinimal, deuxPushup_not_interpolates). Indeed I^+(-1) ∩ I^-(1) = ]0,∞[ ∩ (]-∞,0[∖{-2}) = ∅. The second paragraph (l.322-327) is not restated, and that is disclosed. Marking: the module docstring cites the label unmarked. The bold mark in the docstring of the declaration deux_pushup is minor finding 1. CLOSER FINDINGS CHECKED. (F1, the heart) TRUE. pushUp_of_causallyPlain_of_absolutelyMinimal is [T1Space M] (hmin : C.AbsolutelyMinimal) (hp : C.CausallyPlain) : C.PushUp. It uses the library's AbsolutelyMinimal (Generated.lean:247, the marked def:topological_space_causality_absolutely), CausallyPlain (Properties.lean:55) and PushUp (Properties.lean:69), all marked transcriptions. T1 is the only added hypothesis: Hausdorff implies T1, and second countability is unused. The proof is real, not a trivialisation. interpolatesOn_of_absolutelyMinimalOn applies AbsolutelyMinimalOn.exists_lt_inf (Generated.lean:340) with O = {z}ᶜ. That lemma uses the cover {{z}ᶜ, {x}ᶜ}, open by T1. The first link of the generated chain from x must lie in {z}ᶜ, so its end r ≠ z, and x ≪_U r ≪_U z. Then pushUpOn_of_causallyPlainOn_of_interpolatesOn: given x ≤ y ≪ z and y ≪ w ≪ z, the open set I^+_U(y) ∩ I^-_U(z) ∋ w lies in J^+_U(x), hence in Int J^+_U(x) ⊂ closure I^+_U(x). So it meets I^+_U(x) at some v, and x ≪ v ≪ z (and dually). The result is not vacuous: the timelike line and Minkowski space are T1 and absolutely minimal, with non-empty ≪. Only the ≪ half of absolute minimality is used. The list of absolutely minimal paper examples is right (minkowski_absolutelyMinimal, Static absolutelyMinimal, massive_absolutelyMinimal, generated_absolutelyMinimal). The gluing claim is also right. Under DEC-12, a morphism of C preserves both ≤ and ≪ (Morphism.lean:47). So the colimit in C of a cover's diagram is the generated pair, and a cosheaf (gluing) condition implies AbsolutelyMinimal of M. The conditional 'under a gluing reading the converse half is false for every topological spacetime' therefore follows from the Lean, and 'under the equivalently reading it is witnessed' is deux_pushup. (F2) TRUE. l.318-320 are quoted correctly. pushUp_future_of_interior_Jplus_eq_empty concludes exactly the two future clauses of defi:pushup at x from Int J^+_U(x) = ∅. Both sides are empty because I^+_U(x) and I^+_U(J^+_U(x)) are open subsets of J^+_U(x); the past case follows by dual. A failure x ≤ y ≪ z has z ∈ Int J^+_U(x) and y ∈ I^-_U(z) ⊂ Int J^-_U(z), and the argument above shows its pair y ≪ z cannot interpolate. So the remark's 'silent at a point whose causal future or past has empty interior' cannot produce a counterexample. This is consistent with the rem:pas_plat ledger finding, which uses the same sentence only to say that plainness holds trivially at BTZ points. (F3, density) TRUE: Jminus_subset_closure_Iminus_of_pushUp (LinesReachable.lean:156) and pushUp_does_not_give_hypothesis_b (:474) exist, and the spacelike line has push-up with J^+(x) = {x} ⊄ closure ∅. (F4, which push-up) TRUE: the remark refers to defi:pushup by \ref, and l.209-210 and 290 call plainness 'the push-up property'. The list is non-exhaustive (minor finding 3). QUESTIONS: Q1 is OQ-18 (minor finding 2). Q2 is legitimate: defi:categorie_C (l.232-234) asks only that ≪ be transitive, open and contained in ≤.

findings.what: The gluing question is already open as OQ-18 (registers/DECISIONS.md:174): 'Is the sheaf clause of defi:causalite meant as gluing (≤ generated by covers, i.e. absolute minimality …)?'. The REPORT does not cite it, so the master could open a duplicate OQ. The question also leaves out the paper's own evidence on it. cexemple:point_transparent (ETT.tex:470-480; Lean transparentLine_not_absolutelyMinimalOn) is called 'a topological spacetime' (l.478), and l.470 says absolute minimality is 'not inherited by open subsets'. Its open subset ℝ∖{0} does not glue, so the paper itself rejects the reading 'absolute minimality of every open subset' that the SCOPE gives for gluing. The conditional mathematics is correct, and with DEC-12 (morphisms of C preserve ≪) the colimit identification holds. Only the context put in front of the author is incomplete.
findings.fix: Attach the question to OQ-18 as one more consequence: under gluing, rem:deux_pushup's converse half is false (pushUp_of_causallyPlain_of_absolutelyMinimal). Do not open a new OQ. Add one sentence to the question and the SCOPE: cexemple:point_transparent (l.470-480) is a topological spacetime in the paper whose open subsets need not be absolutely minimal, which supports the 'equivalently' reading under which the remark is certified.

findings.what: Wording. (a) 'its causal relation adds the one pair -2 ≤ -1 to the reflexive closure' is inexact. extLe also adds the consequence -2 ≤ 1 (from -2 ≤ -1 ≪ 1, and -2 ≪ 1 fails since ψ(1) = 2 = φ(-2)), which is the very pair on which push-up fails. ≤ is the reflexive closure of ≪ plus {(-2,-1), (-2,1)}. The extLe docstring ('and its consequences') is right. (b) 'nor any generated causality can serve' should read 'nor any causality generated from absolutely minimal local ones' (theo:causalite_engendre (A), generated_absolutelyMinimal). A precausality generated from non-minimal pieces need not be absolutely minimal. The REPORT says this correctly. (c) The double use of 'push-up' for plainness is cited at l.209-210 and 290. It also occurs at l.130-131 ('we do not assume the push-up property Int(J^±) ⊂ closure I^±'), 141, 216, 297 and 954 (the last already recorded under prop:K_plongement_ordre). Nothing stated is false.
findings.fix: (a) Say 'adds the pair -2 ≤ -1 and its consequence -2 ≤ 1'. (b) Qualify 'generated' as above. (c) Optionally extend the line list in finding 4 to l.130-131, 141, 209-210, 216, 290, 297.
